recognize_zh: Myogenin 免疫染色下，成片的圓形至卵圓形腫瘤細胞大多數呈現棕色細胞核陽性，並被纖維血管間隔分成巢狀，瀰漫強的核陽性支持肺泡型橫紋肌肉瘤。
features: Nests and sheets of crowded round to oval tumor cells separated by pale fibrovascular septa
Nuclear myogenin immunoreactivity in the majority of tumor cells, varying from moderate to strong
Minor subset of nuclei negative (blue hematoxylin counterstain)
Scant cytoplasm with high N:C ratio; mild background cytoplasmic blush
No staining of stromal cells in the septa
describe_en: Myogenin immunohistochemistry shows nests and sheets of small round tumor cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio separated by fibrovascular septa. The majority of tumor cell nuclei show moderate to strong nuclear myogenin staining, with a minor negative subset; stromal cells are negative. Diffuse nuclear myogenin expression confirms skeletal muscle differentiation and is consistent with alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma; FOXO1 rearrangement testing can confirm the subtype.

ddx.vs: Embryonal RMS usually shows only patchy/focal myogenin, whereas diffuse strong nuclear myogenin in most cells favors the alveolar, FOXO1 fusion-positive type.
Ewing sarcoma is myogenin negative with membranous CD99 and nuclear NKX2.2 positivity.
Neuroblastoma is myogenin negative and expresses PHOX2B, synaptophysin and chromogranin.
Lymphoblasts show nuclear TdT rather than myogenin and express CD45 plus B- or T-cell markers.
